newsitem.title: GERMANY: State agency approves rescue plan for German Sket.
newsitem.headline: State agency approves rescue plan for German Sket.

text.p: Germany's BVS, the successor to the Treuhand privatisation agency, on Thursday approved a rescue plan for ailing east German heavy machinery firm Sket which includes cutting three-quarters of its jobs.
The BVS said its decision meant that the continued operation of the company's five remaining units and two subsidiaries was ensured.
The plans are subject to European Commission approval, and the BVS said it would inform the EU of its decision without delay.
The agency also intends to push ahead with plans to privatise the company, now a shadow of its former self, with just 425 of 1,850 jobs surviving.
Sket once employed 18,000 workers as a main supplier to communist eastern Europe but its losses have soaked up over one billion marks ($580 million) in state aid since Germany was unified in 1990.
The BVS is expected to release more than 200 million marks ($115 million) in restructuring funds for Sket given European Commission approval.
